name: Jiankun Lyu
title: Assistant Professor
roster_text: Jiankun Lyu Evnin Family Laboratory of Computational Molecular Discovery Assistant Professor More about this scientist
research: After decades of slow growth in the development of virtual chemical libraries, the advancement of make-on-demand synthesis has enabled their rapid expansion to include billions of molecules. Lyu and his colleagues have taken advantage of this expansion by developing an ultra-large library docking platform, which has been used to screen millions of make-on-demand molecules against seven biological targets and discover novel, potent, and selective ligands. The ultra-large library docking platform represents a huge expansion of the available molecules and chemotypes for chemical biology and drug discovery, readily accessible to the research community.
papers: Covalent targeting of splicing in T cells
AlphaFold2 structures guide prospective ligand discovery

name: Junyue Cao
title: Fisher Center Foundation Associate Professor
roster_text: Junyue Cao Laboratory of Single-Cell Genomics and Population Dynamics Fisher Center Foundation Associate Professor More about this scientist
research: Although current single-cell genomic techniques offer comprehensive profiling of cell states, strategies for manipulating cell states and population dynamics in vivo are still lacking. Another goal of Cao’s lab is to develop methods for cell type-specific manipulation in order to investigate the rules governing cellular functions and cell population homeostasis in vivo. One of these tools, PerturbSci-Kinetics, captures single-cell transcriptional dynamics in response to pooled CRISPR screens targeting various biological processes. This high-throughput technique characterizes elements that govern cell-type-specific gene regulation during RNA synthesis, processing, and degradation. This enable

name: Li Zhao
title: Associate Professor
roster_text: Li Zhao Laboratory of Evolutionary Genetics and Genomics Associate Professor More about this scientist
research: She is particularly interested in de novo genes, which emerge from non-genic DNA. Work in her lab aims to uncover how these and other new genes originate, spread, and contribute to adaptive evolution; to determine how differences in gene expression alter phenotypes; and to identify the genetic basis for adaptation to local environmental conditions.
